entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: T. Rajani
Bench: T. Rajani
 Smt Justice T. Rajani
 Criminal Petition No.222 Of 2020
Order:

This petition is filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C., seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioner, who is accused, in Crime No.131 of 2019 on the file of the Station House Officer, Gudlur Police Station, Prakasam District, registered for the offences under Sections 188, 273, 328, 420 IPC and Sections 59 & 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (FSS Act).
2.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (FSS Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard the counsel for the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent.

3. The counsel for the petitioner submits that in similar circumstances, this Court by virtue of the order dated 13.9.2019 passed in Crl.P.No.5254 of 2019 quashed the proceedings against the accused therein by holding that tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(1)(j) of the FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of the FSS Act.

The order also spells that the counsel for the petitioner therein relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.8.2018, from which, it was seen that the Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the proceedings under IPC and FSS Act.

The order also shows that so far as the offence under Section 188 IPC is concerned, Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C.,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
Like in this case, the said case was also registered suo motu basing on the report of the Sub-Inspector of Police, which is violation of Section 195 Cr.P.C., so far as Section 188 IPC is concerned.
Noting as such, the Court quashed the proceedings against the petitioner in respect of offences under IPC and FSS Act.

4. Hence, in the above terms, the criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings against the petitioner, who is accused, in Crime No.131 of 2019 on the file of the Station House Officer, Gudlur Police Station, Prakasam District, are hereby quashed.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed in consequence.

_ T. RAJANI, J January 21, 2020 YS T Venkateswara Raju vs State Of Andhra Pradesh on 21 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15867413/
